answer: Each agent can post a bond that is forfeited if its identity is later linked to an existing participant by a randomly selected audit using signed payment trails and shared funding sources. The audit does not assume similar writing proves common control; it checks costly, verifiable links. An attacker who creates a swarm must lock up capital for every identity and risks losing those bonds when links are found, making a velvet, dune, or opal persona expensive to multiply rather than merely cheap to name.
